To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the country-of-origin effect is more positive for hedonic products than utilitarian products, more positive for private consumption than public consumption, and more positive for low involvement than high involvement.

the influence of country-of-origin on product evaluations and purchase intentions is stronger for hedonic products than utilitarian products, stronger for consumption in public contexts than private contexts, and stronger for products with high involvement than low involvement.

the influence of country-of-origin effects on product evaluations and purchase intentions is moderated by the product type, consumption context, and involvement, and the moderating effects vary across different cultural orientations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the moderating roles of product type, consumption context, and involvement, which are important in explaining the cultural differences in country-of-Origin effects.
the moderating role of cultural orientations on the relationship between country-of-origin effects and product characteristics, and consumption contexts, and involvement.
how the effects of cultural differences on consumer responses to products from a foreign country are moderated by three product characteristics and three personal cultural orientations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
country-of-origin effects are not universal, and they are not always the same for different products.
the effects of cultural differences on country-of-origin effects are contingent on the interplay among the three product characteristics and the six cultural orientations.
the country-of-origin effects are moderated by the product type, consumption context, and product involvement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
consumers’ cultural orientations interact with product type, consumption context, and product involvement in determining their product evaluation and purchase intention.
country-of-origin effects are not only a function of product and cultural differences, but also the interaction between them.
country-of-origin effects vary by product type, consumption context, and involvement, and the cultural orientations that influence them vary by product type and consumption context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
country-of-origin effects are not a monolithic construct but rather a multifaceted phenomenon that is shaped by product characteristics, consumption context, and personal cultural orientations.
the influence of cultural orientations on country-of-origin effects is contingent on product characteristics, consumption context, and involvement.
the influence of cultural orientations on product evaluations is contingent on the product type, the consumption context, and the level of involvement.
